problem:
The fourth-degree Taylor polynomial of $f(x)$ about $x=-2$ is given by

$$
{P}_{4}(x)=35-60(x+2)+40(x+2)^{2}-11(x+2)^{3}+(x+2)^{4}.
$$

What is ${f}^{‴}(-2)?$
worked_solution:
The coefficient of $(x+2)^{3}$ is given by $\frac{{f}^{‴}(-2)}{3!}.$ Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{f}^{‴}(-2)}{3!} & =-11 \\ \frac{{f}^{‴}(-2)}{6} & =-11 \\ {f}^{‴}(-2) & =-66.\end{aligned}
$$
